records.mutation: chain the second speaker's test through the first speaker's test, and forbid re-deriving cases that caused truncation
records.subagent_summary: Fresh sampling with the incumbent hint scored 1/8 and 5 of 8 truncated at the token cap; every failure enumerated the divisor pairs, noticed each speaker's own value pins the partner within one reading, declared both readings contradictory, and then re-derived the same two cases until truncation or emitted an arbitrary divisor. The incumbent names the label ambiguity but never says the second statement must be evaluated against the first speaker's constraint, so I added that chaining rule plus an explicit ban on re-deriving a case already handled, which is what burned the budget.

records.mutation: keep the ratio/locus setup; replace round-2 circle-fitting recovery with a no-restart rule that treats a failing spot-check as arithmetic in the check, plus a symmetry shortcut and early commit
records.subagent_summary: Seven of eight fresh rollouts were correct in 5k-12k tokens; the single failure derived the roots and the correct structure, then hit an arithmetic slip while solving a general-circle linear system, concluded the problem was contradictory, and burned the full 16384-token cap on ~50 self-doubt cycles without ever committing a result. Round 2 showed that appending recovery/commit discipline to the incumbent setup raised transfer sharply while its explicit circle-fitting route cost train accuracy, so I keep the setup and the discipline but redirect it: treat a conflicting spot-check as a bug in the check, recheck only that line instead of restarting, use symmetry to pin the locus rather than a large linear system, and state the simplified result before the budget runs low.

records.mutation: replace open-ended parameter scanning with a bound-plus-witness optimality certificate that licenses stopping
records.subagent_summary: Four of eight rollouts were correct; all eight reached the right value very early (within the first ~4.5k characters of reasoning), and every failure was purely a truncation failure - it kept re-testing rotations (100+ mentions of rotation, 50-77 'Wait' restarts) until the 16384-token cap hit with the reasoning block still open, so nothing was graded. The incumbent's containment warning is working and is kept, but its 'commit and stop' clause gives no logical reason to stop, so the revision supplies one: a bound valid for all configurations plus a witness attaining it is a complete optimality proof, which makes further scanning provably pointless.

records.mutation: recast the cap as a pointwise root condition on one shared affine target; dissolve the same-piece consecutive-difference identity and justify why the disjoint root budgets add to the asked-for length
records.subagent_summary: Of 8 fresh rollouts only 1 was correct: two hit the 16384-token limit, three declared the task impossible or nearly so by forcing a single piece's own consecutive difference to be constant, and one answered the interpolation point count instead. Most tellingly, one rollout derived the summed per-piece budget and then rejected it because the pattern is a single progression rather than several, so the revision replaces the same-piece difference identity with a pointwise root condition on one shared affine target and states why the disjoint root budgets add to the quantity requested.

records.mutation: replace vague cross-check clause with confirm-constants-early plus a no-guessing, no-restart token-budget rule
records.subagent_summary: Six of eight fresh rollouts were correct in 8-10k tokens; both failures were identical budget deaths at the 16384 cap with finish_reason length, never reaching an area at all. One derived the constants wrongly and only recovered near the cap; the other declared the system unsolvable and burned the remainder substituting guessed numeric values. The incumbent's 'verify with a second, different method' clause invites exactly that extra pass, so I traded it for confirming the constants immediately after solving for them and an explicit ban on numeric guessing and restarting, which targets non-termination generically rather than this setup.

records.mutation: add asserted-determinism (0/1) trap and a one-sample-space rule; name the 'remaining k equally likely to move last' shortcut explicitly
records.subagent_summary: Fresh sampling with the incumbent scored 0/8; seven rollouts terminated normally at 11k-16k tokens and one hit the cap while dithering, so length is only marginal. The second part failed in three recurring ways: two rollouts declared the whole process deterministic and reported certainty or impossibility, four fell back on an asserted 'each of the remaining items is equally likely to be moved last' shortcut giving 1/n or 1/(n-1), and one divided a permutation count by a branch-sequence count. The revision therefore names asserted determinism as a second trap alongside asserted symmetry, calls out the 'equally likely to move last' variant by name, keeps the pin-mechanics and free-versus-forced 1/2 machinery that transferred well in earlier rounds, and adds a same-sample-space check on the ratio.

records.mutation: add off-by-one repair rule for degenerate small cases plus evaluate-don't-expand coefficient extraction
records.subagent_summary: Fresh sampling scored 2 of 8; the 6 failures all hit the token cap, and every one of them stalled at the same place: setting up the reduced instance. They wrote a small case with one condition too many or too few, got a redundant or inconsistent tiny system, then spent thousands of tokens debating whether a solution existed instead of fixing the index range. Two failures additionally burned the remaining budget expanding a long product term by term to extract a single low-order coefficient and kept getting contradictory values, so the revision adds an explicit off-by-one repair rule and tells the student to get that coefficient by evaluating or differentiating at a convenient point rather than expanding.

records.mutation: prepend one-sentence per-unit-vs-total scope-labeling opener to the verbatim incumbent and gloss the markup as an explicit (1+p/100) multiplier
records.subagent_summary: All 8 fresh rollouts scored reward 1 with clean stops at 2.7-5.6k tokens, so train_i is saturated at 1.0 and every remaining gain must come from transfer. The rollouts still burn their first 1-2k tokens oscillating over whether each listed figure is a per-unit amount or a whole-collection total before any arithmetic starts, and the scope-labeling opener is the one mutation whose earlier trial coincided with the best transfer score seen so far, so I add exactly that sentence plus an explicit percent-as-multiplier gloss while leaving the incumbent's train-preserving sentences untouched, since the two prior wholesale rewrites each collapsed train.

records.mutation: force the opposite-sign centered branch with no extra offset, and make the add-the-two-values step a cancellation check that must yield a linear center equation, treating a quadratic/irrational center as a sign bug
records.subagent_summary: Six of eight fresh rollouts were correct, all finishing under 13k tokens by committing early to a single shared-center antisymmetric pair and solving the two given values by adding and subtracting them; both failures ran to the 16384-token cap after mis-parameterizing that ansatz - one carried separate centers/offsets and derived a quadratic for the center with irrational roots, then abandoned the structure for full expansion of the composition, and the other explored inverse/same-sign variants and coefficient matching before ever fixing the signs. The revision therefore pins the exact centered form to use, forbids extra offsets and same-sign branches, and reframes the add-the-two-values step as a cancellation check whose failure signals a sign error to repair in place rather than a cue to expand.

records.mutation: add bijection self-check on hand-built maps and rule that a piecewise split contradicting the clean small-case pattern means a mis-traced case, not a real split
records.subagent_summary: 3 of 8 rollouts were correct; all 5 failures hit the 16384-token cap, and every one of them first got the two smallest cases right, then mis-traced the next-larger case into a claimed period of 2 and spent the rest of the budget oscillating over a piecewise formula it knew could not be the intended single expression. Two of those traces were visibly non-bijective (an element with two images, absurd cycle lengths), which the student read as exotic structure instead of bookkeeping error. The revision therefore keeps the concrete rewrite-the-row discipline but adds a bijection self-check and an explicit rule to distrust the odd larger case rather than the clean pattern, so the student resolves the contradiction and commits instead of looping.
